Draw paired ribbons for two values per span

Source: R/seq_paired_ribbon.R
seq_paired_ribbon.Rd

Draws two thin bands per genomic span: one from the first value y_up upward and one from the second value y_down downward, so equal values touch rather than overlap. All second-value bands are drawn before all first-value bands. Band thickness is a fraction of the top of the track's y range, so it is the same in axis units for every row.

Usage

seq_paired_ribbon(
  data = NULL,
  mapping = NULL,
  aesthetics = aes(),
  legend = NULL,
  legend_labels = NULL,
  legend_extra = NULL,
  show_legend = TRUE,
  legend_position = "canvas_margin",
  legend_side = "right",
  ...
)

Arguments

data

Optional GRanges. Falls back to the parent track's data.

mapping

Optional SeqMap. Fields: x0 (default start), x1 (default end), y_up, y_down (y axis units).

aesthetics

Optional SeqAes. fill_up (default "#D62728"), fill_down ("#1F77B4"), thickness (fraction of the y range top, default 0.012), alpha.

legend

NULL for two automatic rect keys ("first value", "second value"), FALSE for none, or a SeqLegendSpec or list of LegendKey used as given.

legend_labels

Character relabelling the automatic keys, named up and down or given in that order.

legend_extra

List of LegendKey appended to the legend keys.

show_legend

Logical. FALSE suppresses the legend.

legend_position, legend_side

Placement of the legend. Default "canvas_margin", "right".

...

Additional arguments reserved for future use.

Value

A SeqPairedRibbonR6 instance.

Examples

gr <- GenomicRanges::GRanges("chr1", IRanges::IRanges(c(1, 5e5), width = 5e5),
                             a = c(2, 3), b = c(1, 1))
seq_paired_ribbon(gr, map(y_up = a, y_down = b),
                  legend_labels = c(up = "A", down = "B"))
